title: AnnData Export: save measured objects and features
description: Export joined measurements or one object table to h5ad, choose how to handle missing values and retain object metadata.
objectives: Open AnnData Export and select a measured project.
Choose joined or single-table measurements and a missing-value policy.
Export an h5ad file with feature names and object metadata.
prerequisite: Use a project that has completed Measure, or download the measurements example through Annotate. Work on a copy of the project and retain its source images. Use the current nightly build for the normal exporter shown here.

scenes.narration: From Home, open Measure, then choose AnnData Export. Use this tool to save measured objects, their features and their metadata together in an h5ad file.
Select your measured project as Source. For this walkthrough, use a copy of the measurements example available through Annotate. Keep its measurements folder and source images together.
Leave Single table empty to combine the selected tables onto cell rows. Set an output filename ending in h5ad. Keep float32 and gzip for a compact numerical export.
Set Row limit to zero to include every available row. A positive limit is useful for a small first export. Leave Compute UMAP off when you only need the measurement matrix.

Choose keep as the missing-value policy, then press Run. Read the completion message. The joined example contains two thousand three hundred forty-one cell rows and one thousand one hundred thirty-six features.
Set Single table to cell and choose a new output filename. Run again to export the cell measurements alone. Here, the result has two hundred sixty-one features and twenty-eight missing values.

Choose mean to replace missing feature values with observed column means. The export also records their original positions in a missing-value layer. Use this policy when mean imputation fits your downstream analysis.
Choose drop_features to remove columns containing missing values. This example retains all cells and removes four feature columns. Check the retained feature names when comparing exports.
Choose drop_objects to remove rows containing missing feature values. Seven cells are removed here. Consider whether the excluded objects could change your analysis.
Choose nucleus as the single table when you need one row per nucleus. This example produces two thousand six hundred eighty-two nuclei and three hundred forty-one features.

Enable Register artifact to make the output discoverable in the project. Save each policy under a distinct filename and retain its settings. The h5ad file contains measurements and metadata; keep the source images separately.

Open the resulting h5ad file in your downstream analysis and inspect its shape, feature names and object metadata. From Python, run_anndata_export uses the same settings, while build_anndata constructs the data in memory.
